formats.key: Mint721(uint256 tokenId,string tokenURI,Part[] creators,Part[] royalties)Part(address account,uint96 value)
effects: The signature lets the contract mint the NFT `tokenId` with metadata `tokenURI`. The minter is the first creator or an operator it approved, such as Rarible's lazy transfer proxy. The minter picks the recipient `to`, which the signer does not sign.
The token's creators and their shares are written on chain for good. The shares must add up to 10000.
Royalty recipients and their shares are written for the token. The listed accounts receive that share of later sales.
The signature has no expiry and no nonce. It stays valid until the token is minted, or until the first creator burns the unminted tokenId.
The upper 160 bits of tokenId must equal the first creator's address. The NFT is attributed to that creator.
formats.shown: "Lazy Mint ERC-721" with the raw token ID, the token URI, and the creator and royalty accounts and shares as raw values, each listed separately.

findings.title: Mint721 shows creator and royalty shares as raw basis points, not as percentages.
findings.evidence: descriptor: {"path": "royalties.[].value", "label": "Royalties value (10000 = 100%)", "format": "raw"} and same for creators.[].value; ERC721LazyMinimal._saveCreators: require(total == 10000, ...)
findings.fix: Use {"format": "unit", "params": {"base": "%", "decimals": 2}} for creators.[].value and royalties.[].value. Change the labels to "Creator share" and "Royalty share".

findings.title: Mint721 shows creator and royalty accounts as raw addresses, without address names.
Mint721 lists accounts and shares as separate lists, so the signer cannot easily pair each royalty recipient with its share.
findings.evidence: descriptor: fields creators.[].account, creators.[].value, royalties.[].account, royalties.[].value are four separate array fields
findings.fix: Group each Part as one field set, for example a field with path "royalties.[]" and nested fields "account" and "value", so each recipient is shown next to its share.

findings.title: Mint721 intent "Lazy Mint ERC-721" does not say that it sets royalty recipients for every later sale.
findings.evidence: ERC721LazyMinimal.mintAndTransfer: _saveRoyalties(data.tokenId, data.royalties); descriptor intent: "Lazy Mint ERC-721"
findings.fix: Change the intent to "Authorize NFT mint with royalties" and add an interpolatedIntent that names the token ID.

findings.title: Mint721 does not carry the recipient, so the minter or its operator picks who receives the NFT.
findings.evidence: ERC721LazyMinimal.mintAndTransfer(LibERC721LazyMint.Mint721Data memory data, address to): _safeMint(to, data.tokenId); MINT_AND_TRANSFER_TYPEHASH has no recipient member

findings.title: Mint721 has no expiry or nonce. The signature stays valid until the token is minted or burned.
findings.evidence: LibERC721LazyMint: keccak256("Mint721(uint256 tokenId,string tokenURI,Part[] creators,Part[] royalties)Part(address account,uint96 value)"); ERC721BurnableUpgradeableMinimal.burn: _setBurned(tokenId) when the token does not exist

findings.title: Mint721 has no test case, so the rendering of the creators and royalties arrays is never exercised.
findings.fix: Add an EIP-712 test with two creators and one royalty entry, with the expected rendering.
